requirement_text.REQ-425:
MOB-6 in docs/mobile/requirements.md (build-order M6; depends on M2). Built BEFORE MOB-4 (REQ-426..428) -- see the S9 header: the renderers' six states classify this requirement's ApiError. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (refresh-token handling, token clearing).

Hardens lib/api/api_client.dart (created by REQ-421) into the single client:
1. Attach the active tenant's bearer token (REQ-422's iss check).
2. On 401: exactly one silent refresh via flutter_appauth's token refresh, then exactly one retry of the original request; concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh. On refresh failure: clear the tenant's tokens (REQ-422 store) and route to login.
3. Exponential backoff on 5xx for idempotent methods only (GET), bounded attempts; POST is not auto-retried (no duplicate task completion).
4. Normalise every failure to a sealed ApiError type before it leaves lib/api/: at minimum network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden (403), not-found, module-not-available (a 404 on any /api/v1/modules/<id>/ path -- architecture.md §6: absence is 404, not 403, and must not render as a generic not-found), backpressure (429, carrying the Retry-After seconds -- the backend emits 429 from lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex), validation (422 with RFC 9457 field errors), conflict (409), server (5xx after retries).
5. A static guard (apps/mobile/test/guards/), the counterpart of the SPA's raw-fetch-outside-client guard in web/tests/guards/: no file outside lib/api/ imports package:dio or package:http or uses dart:io HttpClient; with a self-test.

task.description:
WF-02 Step 5 for REQ-425. Independently re-run scripts/test_parallel.sh yourself -- do not trust TEST-RUNNER's report alone. Host memory has been borderline this run (last measured ~4.39GB before Step 4, dipping to ~3.47GB mid-run) -- re-check free memory yourself immediately before running and use TEST_PARALLEL_N=2 unless you measure comfortably above ~4GB free; fall back to serial mix test if still tight, and stop rather than retry a third time if reaped twice at the same settings. Also independently re-run flutter analyze && flutter test from apps/mobile/ yourself.

Confirm every one of REQ-425's 7 acceptance criteria is satisfied by checking the actual code/tests directly, not by trusting any prior step's summary -- this includes independently confirming SECURITY-REVIEWER's final PASS (step-02c-security-reviewer-recheck2.json) genuinely closed both cross-tenant token races found across its 3-cycle gate history, by reading the current apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart yourself. Check docs/requirements.yaml and docs/status/requirement_status.v24.yaml for staleness relative to what actually shipped (REQ-425 should currently read status: in_progress, with a started event already appended -- DOC-UPDATER's Step 6, next, is what flips it to done).
acceptance_criteria: a test where the fake server returns 401 once then 200 asserts exactly one refresh call and exactly one retry, and that two concurrent requests both receiving 401 trigger one refresh total
a test where refresh fails asserts the tenant's tokens are deleted from the secure store and the router is at the login route

a test asserts a GET receiving 503 twice then 200 succeeds with increasing delays between attempts (fake clock), a GET receiving 503 on every attempt stops after the maximum attempt count declared as a named constant in lib/api/ and surfaces ApiError server (the test asserts the exact number of requests sent), and a POST receiving 503 is not retried

a test per ApiError variant asserts the mapping from status code/exception, including 404 on /api/v1/modules/exam/x -> module-not-available, 404 elsewhere -> not-found, and 429 with 'Retry-After: 7' -> backpressure(7 seconds)
a test asserts no DioException or SocketException escapes lib/api/ -- the public client API returns or throws only ApiError
the single-client guard fails its self-test fixture (a file under lib/features/ importing package:dio) and passes on the real tree
cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test pass, real output quoted, and SECURITY-REVIEWER signs off before merge

result.summary:
Independent re-verification, first-hand. Host memory measured ~3.15GB free immediately before running (worse than the ~3.47GB dip noted for Step 4) -- ran scripts/test_parallel.sh with TEST_PARALLEL_N=2 first; it was reaped (exit 143, SIGTERM) after ~19 minutes while host-wide free memory bottomed out at ~1.7GB (unrelated processes on this host -- vmmemWSL ~9.8GB, Firefox ~4.9GB, Memory Compression ~2.9GB, Docker -- not anything this run itself leaked). Per the escalation rule (retry once, then fall back to serial), fell back to a plain serial `mix test`, which completed cleanly: `Finished in 2756.6 seconds (28.3s async, 2728.2s sync)` / `Result: 5042 passed (8 properties, 5034 tests), 27 excluded`, exit 0. (TEST-RUNNER's own report claimed 5039/5039 -- the small count difference is consistent with properties/tests being tallied differently, not a regression; both runs are 0-failure.)

Also independently ran `cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test`: `Analyzing mobile... No issues found! (ran in 18.6s)`, then `flutter test`: `+115: All tests passed!`, exit 0 -- matches SECURITY-REVIEWER's own quoted 115/115.

Also independently ran `mix letflow.check.test` (the ISS-0069 dead-default-arg gate) as this role's own instructions separately require, beyond what the task text named. It defaulted to TEST_PARALLEL_N=16 (nproc) and, under the same severe host memory pressure (free memory bottomed at ~1.18GB during this run), one partition reported `Result: 308/309 passed` / `Failed: 1 test`: `Letflow.Routers.MeTest "GET /memberships 200 includes admin-granted memberships..."` failed on `Ecto.InvalidChangesetError` -- a `tenants_slug_index` unique-constraint collision on `insert_tenant!("req384-me-other-#{suffix}")`. This is an unrelated backend Elixir router test (REQ-384 area), not anything under apps/mobile/lib/api/ (REQ-425's entire scope), and it is not the ISS-0069 substring the task exists to gate (grepped the full log for "default values for the optional arguments" -- zero hits, so that specific gate is clean). Confirmed it's a flake and not a real regression two ways: (1) my own serial `mix test` run above, no partitioning, passed this same file with 0 failures as part of its clean 5042/5042; (2) re-ran `mix test test/letflow/routers/me_test.exs --seed 0` in isolation just now -- `Result: 6 passed`, exit 0. Root cause is almost certainly N=16-way partition/suffix collision under this host's current memory pressure, not this diff. Not filing a new queue issue myself per the analysis/implementation split (ORCH or a fresh audit pass should decide whether ISS-0069's own test-parallel gate needs a flakier-suffix fix); flagging it here for visibility since it did surface during this exact validation run.

Acceptance-criteria re-check against the actual current code (apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart, api_error.dart, apps/mobile/test/api/api_client_hardening_test.dart, apps/mobile/test/guards/single_api_client_guard_test.dart), not any prior step's summary:
1. 401-then-200 (exactly one refresh, one retry) and concurrent-401 coalescing: `_RefreshCoordinator.refreshOnce()` shares one in-flight Future; tests '401 refresh-then-retry (AC1)' group present and read directly, including the two-concurrent-401s case (asserts refreshCallCount==1, 4 total requests for 2 paths). SATISFIED.
2. Refresh-failure token clearing + login routing: `_RefreshCoordinator._handleFailure` deletes tokens via `_tokenStore.delete(realmUrl)` and calls `_routeToLogin()`; 'refresh failure (AC2)' test group covers both the invalid-grant case and the no-refresh-token-stored case. SATISFIED.
3. GET-only 5xx backoff, bounded attempts, POST never retried: `kMaxServerRetryAttempts = 3` is a named top-level const in api_client.dart; `backoffDelayFor` doubles from `kBaseServerRetryDelay` (200ms); `post()` calls `_sendWithBackoff(..., allowServerRetry: false)`. Tests assert exact delay sequence [200ms, 400ms], exact request count == kMaxServerRetryAttempts on persistent 503, and a POST-503 sends exactly 1 request with zero delays. SATISFIED.
4. ApiError variant mapping: `classifyError` in api_error.dart covers 401/403/404(module vs plain via `_modulePathPattern`)/429(`_parseRetryAfter`, defaults to 1)/422(`_parseFieldErrors`, RFC 9457)/409/5xx/catch-all; tests cover every branch including the exact `/api/v1/modules/exam/x` -> moduleId 'exam' case and a bare `/api/v1/modules/exam` (no trailing segment) correctly falling through to NotFoundError. SATISFIED.
5. No raw DioException/SocketException escapes lib/api/: `_sendWithBackoff` and `_handleUnauthorized` both catch DioException and rethrow only via `classifyError`/typed ApiError; test group 'no raw transport exception escapes lib/api/ (AC5)' confirms a connectionError DioException wrapping a SocketException maps to NetworkUnavailableError and that no ApiError variant is itself a DioException. SATISFIED.
6. Static single-client guard: single_api_client_guard_test.dart has a pure `checkSingleApiClientBoundary` checker, a real-tree test, and three distinct self-test fixtures (dio import, http import, dart:io HttpClient construction) each firing exactly one violation outside lib/api/, plus a fourth self-test confirming zero violations for the same import *inside* lib/api/ (the sanctioned exemption). SATISFIED.
7. flutter analyze && flutter test pass with quoted output + SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off: both re-run above by me directly (not trusted from any report); SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-02c-security-reviewer-recheck2.json is COMPLETED/PASS, and I independently re-read the current api_client.dart myself (823 lines) and traced both fixed races: rework 1 (_RefreshCoordinator._doRefresh re-checks `_activeRealm.currentRealmUrl`/`clientId` against the captured realmUrl both before persisting refreshed tokens and in its catch branch, so a tenant switch/logout racing the refresh network call cannot resurrect old tokens or serve the wrong tenant -- confirmed by the 'cross-tenant refresh race (rework 1)' test group, both sub-cases passing) and rework 2 (`_bearerInterceptor` independently re-verifies `_kIssuedForRealmKey` against `activeRealm.currentRealmUrl` read fresh at token-attach time on a retry-dispatch pass, rejecting via `_CrossTenantRetryAbortedException` before any token is attached or the transport layer is reached -- confirmed by the 'cross-tenant retry-dispatch race (rework 2)' test, which registers a probe interceptor ahead of the bearer interceptor to land the tenant switch exactly in the post-refresh-success/pre-token-attach window and asserts the retry never reaches the fake adapter). Also confirmed REVIEWER's step-02d-reviewer.json is COMPLETED/PASS ('idiom/scope gate closed, REQ-425 has security PASS and reviewer PASS'). All 7 SATISFIED.

docs/requirements.yaml REQ-425 entry and docs/status/requirement_status.v24.yaml both read status: in_progress with a 2026-09-29T11:21:12Z 'started' event already appended and no 'done' event yet -- consistent with the task's expectation that DOC-UPDATER (Step 6) is what flips status, not stale.

Verdict: PASS. No blocking issues found in REQ-425's own scope.
issues: Unrelated flake observed during this validation's mix letflow.check.test run (N=16 partitions under severe host memory pressure): Letflow.Routers.MeTest 'GET /memberships 200 includes admin-granted memberships...' hit a tenants_slug_index unique-constraint collision. Confirmed not a REQ-425 regression (serial full suite and an isolated re-run of the file both pass cleanly). Not filed as a queue issue per the analysis/implementation split -- flagging for whoever next touches ISS-0069's test-parallel gate or REQ-384's tenant-slug fixture generation to consider whether high-N partitioning needs a more collision-resistant slug suffix.
